title: Disclosure of sensitive health and location telemetry by the wearer
description: By wearing the device continuously, the user discloses raw sensor telemetry including heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps to the wearable. These data can reveal intimate facts such as health status, routines, places visited, and daily habits.
assumptions: The wearable receives and can access/store the raw telemetry generated during use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may differ.

title: Linkability of telemetry records over time
description: Continuous transmission of telemetry with timestamps and persistent device/user context can allow multiple observations on this flow to be linked to the same wearer over time, enabling reconstruction of routines and longitudinal profiles.
assumptions: The flow is repeated over time and carries stable or correlatable context such as device identity, timing, or characteristic sensor patterns.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit; exact LINDDUN Pro node may be more specific to repeated observations or persistent identifiers.

title: Identifiability of the wearer from location and biometric patterns
description: Even if explicit identifiers are absent, GPS traces, timestamps, gait/activity patterns, and heart-rate-related telemetry can make the wearer identifiable by correlating home/work locations or distinctive behavioral/biometric patterns.
assumptions: An observer or recipient can correlate telemetry with external knowledge or prior records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may distinguish direct vs indirect identification.

title: Inference of sensitive attributes by the wearable device
description: On receipt, the wearable can process the telemetry to infer sensitive information beyond the raw data, such as exercise habits, sleep/wake cycles, medical conditions, stress levels, or frequently visited sensitive locations.
assumptions: The device software performs analytics or stores sufficient data for later inference.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; exact LINDDUN Pro node for inferred/derived sensitive data may differ.

title: Unawareness of continuous collection and its privacy implications
description: The wearer may be insufficiently aware of the extent, frequency, granularity, or consequences of continuous collection of heart rate, movement, location, and timestamps by the device.
assumptions: Not all collection details, retention, or downstream uses are made salient to the wearer at the moment of collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact subtree may separate lack of transparency from lack of user control.

title: Non-compliance risk from collecting more data than necessary
description: Continuous capture of GPS position, timestamps, and detailed telemetry may exceed what is necessary for some wearable functions, creating risk of violating data minimization, purpose limitation, or valid-consent requirements.
assumptions: Some device features could operate with less granular, less frequent, or less extensive data collection.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; exact LINDDUN Pro compliance subtree may use different numbering.

title: Stable device identifier enables linking of sessions and traces
description: The wearable shares a persistent device id together with exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps. This allows records from multiple syncs to be linked to the same person or device over time, building a longitudinal activity profile.
assumptions: The device id is stable across sync events and visible to the app.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ depending on the threat-tree variant used.

title: Data in transit can identify the user through device id and location trail
description: The flow contains direct or near-direct identifiers such as device id plus highly identifying GPS traces and timestamps. If exposed on the communication channel, these data can identify or single out the user.
assumptions: An attacker or unintended party can observe the sync traffic or its payload.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; identification may map to a more specific subtree in some LINDDUN Pro catalogs.

title: Sensitive activity and location data are disclosed during sync
description: Exercise sessions and GPS traces reveal sensitive behavioral and location information. If the sync channel is insufficiently protected, the contents may be disclosed to eavesdroppers or intermediaries.
assumptions: Transport protection may be absent, weak, or bypassed in some contexts.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact disclosure subtree may vary.

title: Communication metadata can link device and app interactions
description: Even aside from payload contents, repeated sync timing, endpoints, packet sizes, and frequency can allow an observer to link multiple communications to the same wearable-app pair and infer routines.
assumptions: An observer can access network metadata for repeated sync events.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for linkability via communication metadata.

title: Companion app can identify the user from received data
description: On receipt, the app can combine device id, repeated exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps to identify or single out the user, even if no explicit real name is included in this flow.
assumptions: The app has or can derive account, phone, or other contextual data to associate the sync with a person.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact identification subnode may differ.

title: Companion app may disclose detailed history beyond what is necessary
description: The app receives full sensor batches including precise GPS traces and timestamps. Storing, exposing, or reusing this detailed history in the app environment can disclose sensitive habits, routes, home/work locations, and health-related behavior.
assumptions: The app stores or makes accessible the raw synced data beyond immediate display needs.
uncertainty_note: Approximate disclosure node id for recipient-side exposure/storage.

title: Secondary use of synced data may exceed user expectations
description: The companion app may use synced exercise and location data for analytics, personalization, advertising, or sharing with other components in ways not expected by the user at the time of device sync.
assumptions: Purpose limitation and in-app transparency/controls are incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for unawareness/unexpected processing.

title: Collection of precise GPS traces may be unnecessary for core sync purpose
description: The app may collect or retain more detail than needed for basic synchronization or activity summaries, such as raw GPS traces, exact timestamps, or persistent identifiers, creating a non-compliance/data-minimization risk.
assumptions: Some app functions could operate with reduced precision, aggregation, or pseudonymous identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for non-compliance with data minimization/purpose limitation.

title: User may be unable to repudiate having performed a session at a place and time
description: The app's receipt and storage of timestamped exercise sessions and GPS traces can create strong evidence that a user was at a specific location at a specific time, limiting plausible denial if records are later used against the user.
assumptions: The app stores the synced records with sufficient integrity and association to the user/device.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; repudiation coverage varies across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Direct identification through self-entered health and body data
description: The wearer manually provides calorie intake, meal details, and weight entries that can directly identify or strongly single out them when tied to their app account or device profile.
assumptions: The app account or device context can associate entries with a specific individual.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Linkability of repeated diet and weight logs over time
description: Repeated manual entries about meals, calories, and weight create a longitudinal pattern that can be linked across sessions, enabling correlation of records belonging to the same wearer.
assumptions: The app stores entries under a persistent account, identifier, or device context.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; threat applicability is strong even if exact subtree label differs.

title: Detectability of sensitive health-related behavior from the act of logging
description: The act of submitting meal, calorie, and weight information reveals that the wearer is tracking diet or weight-management behavior, which may itself be sensitive.
assumptions: Observers at the recipient or elsewhere can infer behavior from the submission event.
uncertainty_note: Exact detectability node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Linkability via transmission metadata
description: Even if content is protected, metadata on this flow such as timing, frequency, device/app identifiers, or network endpoints may allow linking multiple submissions to the same wearer.
assumptions: Transmission or app telemetry exposes stable metadata.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; chosen as best fit for metadata-based linkability on the flow.

title: Detectability of logging events in transit
description: Traffic characteristics or local device/network observations may reveal when the wearer logs meals or weight, exposing sensitive routines even without reading the content.
assumptions: An observer can see network or device-level signaling associated with submission.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id uncertain; threat is based on event/traffic observability.

title: Linkability of nutrition and weight entries with other app data
description: On receipt, the companion app can link calorie, meal, and weight entries with account data, device identifiers, activity history, or wearable data, creating a richer profile of the wearer.
assumptions: The app has access to persistent identifiers and additional user datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory.

title: Identification through combined profile data at the app
description: The app may identify the wearer from the submitted entries when combined with account registration details, device identifiers, or other profile attributes.
assumptions: The app maintains user accounts or other identifying context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact subtree may differ.

title: Disclosure of sensitive dietary and weight information
description: The companion app receives and processes highly sensitive personal data about diet, eating habits, and body weight, creating risk of privacy harm if exposed internally or beyond expected use.
assumptions: The app stores or further processes the submitted values.
uncertainty_note: Using D as disclosure of information; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Unawareness of secondary use of manually logged health data
description: The wearer may not be fully aware that manually entered meal, calorie, and weight data could be used for profiling, analytics, recommendations, or sharing beyond immediate logging functionality.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-app explanations may be incomplete or not salient at entry time.
uncertainty_note: Exact unawareness subtree id is approximate.

title: Non-compliance risk for processing health-related manual entries
description: Because meal, calorie, and especially weight data can be health-related or sensitive, the app's collection and processing may violate data minimization, transparency, consent, or purpose-limitation obligations if not properly governed.
assumptions: Applicable privacy law or platform rules treat these data as personal or potentially sensitive.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate and depends on the applicable compliance framework.

title: Excessive collection of health-log data by the app
description: The mobile app may write more health data than is necessary for the stated purpose, such as detailed calorie intake, full weight history, and granular exercise-session records when only summaries are needed. The act of sending this full dataset to storage creates a disclosure risk.
assumptions: Assumes some app features could function with less granular or less frequent data than is written to the store.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure via oversharing/minimisation failure; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Linkability through persistent identifiers and repeated health-log uploads
description: Repeated writes from the same app instance to the health log store can be linked together via stable account IDs, device IDs, session tokens, or consistent metadata, allowing multiple health events over time to be tied to the same individual profile.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries or is accompanied by stable identifiers or metadata that persist across uploads.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability from data/metadata in transit; exact subtree may vary.

title: Identifiability from health-log content or metadata in transit
description: Even if direct identifiers are limited, the combination of weight history, exercise patterns, timestamps, and other metadata on this flow may uniquely identify a user or make re-identification feasible when combined with other data.
assumptions: Assumes the transmitted records include timestamps, account references, or sufficiently distinctive behavioral/health patterns.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability due to quasi-identifiers and metadata; exact node may differ.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health logs at the store
description: Once received, the health log store may expose sensitive health information to unauthorized internal components, administrators, analytics functions, or attackers if access controls, segregation, or encryption are insufficient.
assumptions: Assumes the datastore persists the logs and that access control or encryption weaknesses are plausible.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure caused by storage/processing at destination; exact node naming may differ.

title: Secondary use of health logs beyond user expectations
description: The health log store may enable use of stored calorie, weight, and exercise data for analytics, profiling, recommendations, marketing, or sharing with other services beyond the purpose the user understood when entering the data.
assumptions: Assumes governance or purpose limitation controls are incomplete or broad downstream uses are possible.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unintended/secondary use at destination; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Insufficient transparency or consent for storing detailed health logs
description: The destination may store detailed health logs without adequately informing the user about what categories are stored, retention periods, downstream recipients, or optionality, resulting in non-compliance with consent or transparency obligations.
assumptions: Assumes health data is regulated/sensitive and notice-consent mechanisms may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance related to transparency/consent at destination; exact node may differ.

title: Failure to minimize retention of historical health logs
description: The health log store may retain calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions indefinitely or longer than necessary, increasing exposure and sensitivity over time.
assumptions: Assumes retention limits or deletion schedules are absent, weak, or not enforced.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability/discoverability from retained stored data; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may differ because retention can also be modeled under disclosure-related branches.

title: Excessive disclosure of precise location traces by the app
description: The mobile app shares fine-grained GPS traces with timestamps to the store. This may disclose more personal data than necessary, revealing sensitive habits, places visited, routines, and potentially special-category inferences.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for disclosure at source may differ.

title: Linkability of records in transit via persistent identifiers and repeated uploads
description: Repeated uploads of timestamped GPS traces from the same app/session/account can be linked together on the flow, enabling correlation of multiple traces to the same individual or device.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; threat clearly concerns linkability of repeated location-trace transmissions.

title: Identifiability from location-time patterns in transit
description: Even if explicit identifiers are absent, precise spatiotemporal traces can uniquely identify a person through home/work locations, routine paths, or rare visits observable from the transmitted data.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may vary in LINDDUN Pro; identifiability from quasi-identifying location data is the core issue.

title: Over-retention and broad availability of stored location history
description: Once received, the location history store may retain raw traces indefinitely or make them broadly accessible for analytics or secondary uses, increasing disclosure risk of sensitive movement history.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for disclosure caused by destination-side storage/processing.

title: Linkability across stored location-history entries
description: The destination can combine multiple uploaded traces over time, linking records across days, devices, or contexts to build a longitudinal movement profile for the same person.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; destination-side correlation of stored records is the intended threat.

title: Identification of the user from stored history
description: The store can identify or single out the user from accumulated location history by inferring home address, workplace, regular routes, or co-location patterns, even if direct identifiers are minimized.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; destination-side identification from stored traces is the intended threat.

title: Unawareness of storage and downstream use of location history
description: Users may be unaware that the app writes detailed GPS traces with timestamps to a persistent history store, including how long data is kept, who can access it, and what analyses are performed.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is an unawareness threat caused by destination-side processing/storage practices.

title: Non-compliance risk from storing precise location history without adequate legal basis or minimization
description: Persistently storing precise timestamped location traces may violate privacy obligations if consent, purpose limitation, minimization, retention limits, transparency, or user rights handling are inadequate.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id for non-compliance is approximate; applicability depends on jurisdiction and system controls.

title: Cross-session health logs enable linkage of records to the same individual
description: By disclosing calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions to the analytics service, the data store enables the recipient to correlate multiple records over time and link them to the same user profile or device/account.
assumptions: The logs contain a stable account, device, pseudonym, or consistent behavioral pattern that allows correlation across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Health and lifestyle logs may identify the individual
description: The combination of weight history, exercise patterns, and calorie logs can be sufficiently distinctive to identify a person directly or indirectly when shared with the analytics service.
assumptions: Either explicit identifiers are present, or quasi-identifiers/behavioral uniqueness make re-identification feasible.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit from memory.

title: Analytics infers sensitive health conditions from longitudinal logs
description: On receipt of the logs, the analytics service may derive or infer sensitive information such as obesity trends, eating disorders, chronic conditions, or other health-related states beyond the raw data originally recorded.
assumptions: The service performs condition analysis or profiling over time, not merely simple aggregation.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may vary in LINDDUN Pro; threat applicability is strong.

title: Use of logs for health-condition analysis may exceed user expectations
description: The destination processes calorie, weight, and exercise logs for health-condition analysis, which may constitute secondary use or processing beyond the purpose the user reasonably expected when entering the logs.
assumptions: Users were not clearly informed that their logs would be analyzed longitudinally for condition inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact purpose-deviation subtree label may differ.

title: Users may be unaware of longitudinal analytics on their logs
description: If the analytics service reads and analyzes logs across sessions without clear notice, users may not understand that their historical health data is being processed for condition analysis.
assumptions: Transparency notices or in-product explanations are absent, unclear, or incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate from memory.

title: Processing special-category health data may lack a valid legal basis or consent
description: Health-condition analysis on weight, exercise, and calorie logs can involve special-category health data processing. If the analytics service lacks explicit consent, another valid legal basis, or required safeguards, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Applicable law treats inferred or analyzed health-condition data as regulated sensitive data.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate; legal applicability depends on jurisdiction and system context.

title: Flow metadata can link datastore access events over time
description: Even if payload contents are protected, repeated reads from the health log store to the analytics service can expose metadata such as timing, frequency, and volume that links analysis events to the same user or cohort across sessions.
assumptions: An observer or intermediary can access communication metadata for DF6.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit flow-level linkage node id from memory.

title: Cross-session linkage of location records to the same individual
description: The analytics service queries location history across sessions, enabling records from multiple sessions to be linked together and associated with the same person or device over time. This supports construction of a longitudinal profile beyond a single interaction.
assumptions: Location history records are keyed or otherwise queryable by a persistent identifier, account, device identifier, or stable pseudonym.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability via combining records across contexts/sessions.

title: Identification of an individual from location history patterns
description: Daily routine and movement patterns derived from historical location traces can uniquely identify a person, even if direct identifiers are absent, because home/work locations and habitual routes are often highly distinctive.
assumptions: The service has access to sufficiently granular location history or can combine derived patterns with other available attributes.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; threat clearly concerns identifiability from quasi-identifying mobility patterns.

title: Inference of sensitive habits and routines
description: By analyzing location history across sessions, the service can infer private information such as home address, workplace, religious attendance, medical visits, political activity, social relationships, and other sensitive behavioral patterns that were not explicitly provided by the user.
assumptions: Analytics outputs or internal models are retained or used for profiling, personalization, or decision-making.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure/inference of sensitive information from observed data.

title: Secondary use of location history for behavioral profiling
description: Location history originally collected for operational or user-facing purposes may be reused by the analytics service to derive daily routines and movement patterns, which can exceed the user's reasonable expectations or original purpose of collection.
assumptions: The original collection context did not clearly and specifically communicate this analytics use, or user consent/preferences do not cover it.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; the threat is clear as purpose creep/secondary use at the destination.

title: Processing beyond user consent or stated purpose
description: If the analytics service derives routine and movement patterns without valid consent, adequate transparency, or another appropriate legal basis, the processing may be non-compliant with privacy obligations governing purpose limitation, transparency, and lawful processing.
assumptions: Applicable policy or regulation requires explicit notice, consent, or another legal basis for this form of profiling.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance due to profiling and purpose limitation concerns; exact node id may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Linkability via query and transfer metadata
description: Even at the data-flow level, metadata about repeated queries from the analytics service to the location history store—such as timing, frequency, subject identifiers, or query scope—can reveal that multiple sessions or records relate to the same individual and support longitudinal tracking.
assumptions: Flow metadata is observable to infrastructure components, logs, or intermediaries, or is retained for operational monitoring.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is a data-in-transit/meta-data-based linkability threat.

title: Inferred health-condition risk indicators may identify or single out the user
description: By sending inferred risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags to the mobile app, the analytics service discloses highly distinctive health-related inferences that can identify or single out the data subject, especially when combined with the app account or device context.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for identifiability via disclosed content; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Disclosure of sensitive inferred health information to the app
description: The analytics service shares sensitive inferred data about possible health conditions, routines, and trends with the app. If the app context is less protected than the analytics environment, this transfer increases the risk of exposing special-category health information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure of sensitive personal data; exact subtree numbering may vary.

title: Flow contents and metadata can link analytics results to a specific user or device
description: Even if transport security is present, the existence, timing, frequency, and size of messages carrying inferred insights can help link a particular app session or device to a specific analytics profile or health-monitoring pattern.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability through communication metadata in transit; exact node id may differ.

title: Interception of inferred insights in transit
description: If the flow is insufficiently protected in transit, an attacker observing network traffic could learn sensitive health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, or trend flags.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure during transmission; exact node id may differ.

title: App-side exposure of inferred insights to unauthorized viewers
description: Once received by the mobile app, inferred insights may be displayed in notifications, cached locally, exposed through screenshots, backups, logs, or accessible UI states, disclosing sensitive health information to other people or apps with access to the device.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure at the recipient through storage/display; exact node id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that the app receives and uses inferred health insights
description: The app may present analytics outputs without making it clear that these are inferred health-condition risk indicators derived from prior data processing, reducing user awareness of what personal information is being processed and shown.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency at the recipient; exact node id may differ.

title: Use of inferred health insights may exceed user expectations or consent
description: The app may use received risk indicators, summaries, and trend flags for secondary purposes such as personalization, nudging, profiling, or sharing onward, beyond the purposes the user understood or consented to.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance/purpose creep at the destination; exact node id may differ.

title: App reveals highly sensitive inferred health-condition indicators to the user interface
description: The mobile app actively discloses inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals and trend information to the wearer. Because these are sensitive health inferences, displaying them can identify the user's health status or suspected condition to anyone who can view the screen, including people nearby or anyone with temporary access to the device.
assumptions: The dashboard content is visible on-screen without additional privacy-preserving controls such as masking, re-authentication, or private-view mode.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of sensitive personal attributes to an unauthorized viewer via presentation to the user; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary by catalog wording.

title: Dashboard output exposes private health inferences to shoulder surfers or other unintended viewers
description: By presenting condition indicators and trends in the app dashboard, the source process may disclose personal and potentially stigmatizing information to unintended recipients in the user's environment. This is a classic information disclosure risk caused by the act of sharing/displaying the data.
assumptions: The user may open the app in public or shared spaces, or the device may be unlocked and visible to others.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for unauthorized disclosure during communication/presentation; exact subtree label may differ.

title: Risk indicators may be presented without sufficient transparency or explainability
description: The app may show inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals without clearly explaining how they were derived, how reliable they are, or what data sources contributed. This can leave the user unaware of the extent and meaning of profiling performed about them.
assumptions: The dashboard emphasizes outputs but may not provide explanation, confidence, provenance, or limitations of the inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency around privacy-relevant processing and inference generation.

title: Sensitive health inferences may be shown without valid, specific consent for this disclosure
description: Displaying inferred condition indicators to the user may exceed the scope of consent originally given for collecting wearable/app data, especially if the user did not explicitly agree to generation and presentation of eating-disorder or diabetes risk assessments. The privacy threat arises from sharing secondary inferences back to the user without appropriate consent or expectation management.
assumptions: Consent may have covered wellness tracking generally but not sensitive-condition inference or presentation of diagnostic-like indicators.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for missing or invalid consent regarding a specific privacy-relevant processing purpose; exact node id may differ.

title: Notifications or transmission metadata may disclose sensitive app usage context
description: If the dashboard content or related push/update traffic generates visible notifications, previews, or observable metadata, third parties could infer that the user is receiving eating-disorder or diabetes risk information even without seeing the full content. The threat arises on the flow through exposure of communication metadata or message previews.
assumptions: The flow may involve network delivery, push notifications, lock-screen previews, or observable app traffic patterns associated with dashboard updates.
uncertainty_note: This depends on implementation details of the flow and whether notifications/metadata are exposed; node id is approximate.

title: Excessive disclosure of full health and location dataset to third-party cloud provider
description: The Health Analytics Service shares the full health and location dataset, along with analytics data and models, with an external cloud hosting provider for hosting and replication. Sending the full dataset may disclose more personal data than is necessary for the hosting purpose, especially highly sensitive health and precise location data.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider does not strictly need identifiable full-fidelity health and location records for all hosting/replication operations, or that minimisation/pseudonymisation is not applied before transfer.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for over-disclosure/excessive sharing; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may vary.

title: Transfer to cloud provider may be incompatible with original collection purpose or user expectations
description: Replicating the full health and location dataset to a third-party cloud provider may go beyond the purpose users reasonably expected when their data was collected, particularly if users were not clearly informed that a separate external provider would host and replicate sensitive data.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation, transparency, or processor-transfer constraints were not fully addressed in notices, contracts, or consent where required.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for non-compliance related to purpose limitation/transparency/third-party transfer.

title: Cloud provider can link health and location records across datasets, tenants, or services
description: Once the cloud provider receives hosted analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset, it may be able to correlate records using persistent identifiers, account metadata, storage patterns, or operational telemetry. This can enable linking of a person's sensitive health data with location history and potentially with other datasets accessible to the provider.
assumptions: Assumes the provider has visibility into stored content or rich metadata and that technical/contractual controls do not fully prevent such correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability caused by recipient-side correlation; exact subtree may differ.

title: Cloud provider may identify individuals from hosted health and location data
description: The combination of full health records and location data is highly identifying. Even if direct identifiers are reduced, the cloud provider may be able to re-identify individuals from quasi-identifiers, unique movement patterns, account metadata, or model artifacts derived from the data.
assumptions: Assumes data is not strongly anonymised and the provider can access plaintext data or sufficiently revealing metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability at the recipient; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Replication and storage at the cloud provider increase exposure of sensitive data
description: Hosting and replication at the destination can multiply copies of the full health and location dataset across regions, backups, and storage layers. This broadens internal access paths and increases the amount of sensitive personal data exposed within the provider environment.
assumptions: Assumes replication creates additional accessible copies and retention boundaries are not tightly constrained.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure through storage/replication at the destination.

title: Individuals may be unaware that a third-party cloud provider hosts and replicates their sensitive data
description: If the use of the cloud hosting provider is not visible to data subjects, they may not understand who processes their health and location data, where it is stored, or that multiple replicated copies exist. This reduces users' awareness of the processing context and associated privacy implications.
assumptions: Assumes notices or interfaces do not clearly disclose third-party hosting and replication arrangements.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact subtree may differ.

title: Cloud hosting and replication may violate data residency, retention, or processor-control obligations
description: A third-party cloud provider may replicate the full health and location dataset across jurisdictions or retain copies in backups and replicas longer than permitted. This can create non-compliance with contractual, regulatory, or policy obligations governing sensitive health and location data.
assumptions: Assumes cross-border replication, backup retention, or processor oversight controls may be insufficiently constrained.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for compliance risks around residency/retention/processor management; exact node id may vary.

title: Transfer metadata can reveal linkage between analytics service and sensitive dataset hosting
description: Even if transport security protects content, metadata about the transfer itself—such as endpoints, timing, volume, frequency, and replication patterns—can reveal that the health analytics service is sending large sensitive datasets to the cloud provider. This may enable linkage between the service, particular processing activities, and categories of individuals or cohorts.
assumptions: Assumes network or operational observers can access communication metadata or logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via communication metadata on the flow.

title: Data in transit may enable identification if intercepted or insufficiently protected
description: Because the flow contains the full health and location dataset, interception or exposure during transfer could directly identify individuals or make them readily identifiable from the sensitive content and associated metadata.
assumptions: Assumes transport encryption, key management, or endpoint protections may be weak or misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability arising from in-transit exposure; exact subtree may differ.
